name: Local Ambient Occlusion
text:
# Local Ambient Occlusion
## Overview
Local Ambient Occlusion methods estimate indirect illumination blocking in volume rendering by sampling local density or stochastic rays around a point, avoiding global shadow maps or precomputed buffers [G]. Unlike siblings that rely on [Signed Distance Fields](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) [2527-ambient-occlusion-via-sdf-geometry.md] or voxel buffers [6646-voxel-ambient-occlusion.md], these techniques compute occlusion on-the-fly or via lightweight per-pixel accumulation, adapting to the volume's internal density structure [S1, unofficial].
## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of evaluating visibility or illumination at a specific point $\mathbf{p}$ within or on the boundary of a volume, based on a light source direction $\mathbf{l}$ or environment [Parent](5936-ambient-occlusion-via-geometry-neighbors.md).
## Subtopics

### [Local Ambient Occlusion for Volume Rendering](4300-local-ambient-occlusion-for-volume-rendering.md)
Calculates ambient occlusion by integrating opacity over the local vicinity's normal distribution, accelerated by approximating the Transfer Function as piecewise linear segments [4300-local-ambient-occlusion-for-volume-rendering.md]. It assumes CT values follow a normal distribution to estimate occlusion probability, reducing computation from iterating over all CT values to the number of TF segments [4300-local-ambient-occlusion-for-volume-rendering.md]. Choose when high performance is needed for CT data with known statistical distributions [G].

### [Local Ambient Occlusion (LAO)](4502-local-ambient-occlusion-lao.md)
Estimates [local occlusion](#4300-local-ambient-occlusion-for-volume-rendering.md) by sampling the volume along random directions around the light vector, weighted by distance [4502-local-ambient-occlusion-lao.md]. It differs from global shadowing methods by approximating indirect illumination through incremental, per-pixel accumulation of visibility samples, allowing dynamic [interaction](#41-interaction.md) with the volume's internal density structure without precomputed global buffers [4502-local-ambient-occlusion-lao.md]. Choose when a soft, noise-based approximation of ambient occlusion is acceptable and precomputation is undesirable [G].

### [Feature-Driven Ambient Occlusion](8903-feature-driven-ambient-occlusion.md)
Computes ambient occlusion separately for identified features to prevent overdarkening of internal layers caused by inter-occlusions from neighboring features, while preserving auto-occlusions [8903-feature-driven-ambient-occlusion.md]. It neglects inter-occlusions between features to prevent overdarkening while keeping auto-occlusions [8903-feature-driven-ambient-occlusion.md]. Choose for multi-layer volumes where preserving the visibility of internal structures is critical [G].

### Lambertian Lighting with AO and Shadows
Combines Lambertian diffuse shading with Local Ambient Occlusion and Soft Shadows contributions to produce the final volume color [S1, unofficial]. The normal is computed from the gradient: `n = normalize(grad);` [S1, unofficial]. The half vector is calculated as `halfVector = normalize(vLight - position);` [S1, unofficial]. The Lambertian term is `nDotL = max(dot(n, halfVector), 0.0);` [S1, unofficial]. The base color is retrieved from the transfer function: `color = getColor(value, gradientMagnitude(grad));` [S1, unofficial]. The color is mixed with [LAO](#4502-local-ambient-occlusion-lao.md) darkening: `color = mix(color, color * vec4(0.15, 0.18, 0.32, 1.0), LAOContribution.r * uLAOWeight);` [S1, unofficial]. The color is mixed with Shadow darkening: `color = mix(color, color * vec4(0.15, 0.18, 0.22, 1.0), uSoftShadowsContribution.r * uShadowsWeight);` [S1, unofficial].

### Deferred Shading for Ambient Occlusion
Renders world position and surface normal pixels of the image from the current point of view to a buffer [S2]. It executes AO computation in the fragment shader on each pixel using the underlying normal and position [S2]. This avoids evaluating the computation for hidden geometry [S2].
